key_insight: RoSHI combines low-cost sparse IMUs with egocentric Project Aria glasses to recover full 3D human pose and body shape in a metric global frame, trading off neither portability nor global consistency for robustness to occlusion.
problem_solved: Collecting rich, long-horizon human interaction data in the wild is hampered by systems that sacrifice portability, occlusion robustness, or global consistency; RoSHI addresses all three simultaneously to enable scalable real-world data capture.
method: Hybrid hardware: fuse sparse body-mounted IMUs with egocentric cameras (Project Aria) to exploit complementary strengths (inertial continuity + visual context).
Sensor fusion pipeline: temporally align and fuse IMU and visual cues to estimate full 3D kinematics and body shape in a metric global coordinate frame.
Global registration & tracking: maintain consistent, long-horizon pose in world coordinates to tolerate occlusion and enable multi-scene aggregation.
impact: Enables scalable collection of consistent, long-horizon human motion datasets in natural settings, improving training data quality for robot learning, imitation, and human-robot interaction research.
visual_elements: System diagram: wearable stack showing Project Aria glasses + sparse IMU nodes and data flow arrows (camera → fusion → global pose).
Pipeline flowchart: stages for synchronization, sensor fusion, body-shape estimation, and global registration.
Before/after examples: egocentric video frames with occlusion vs. reconstructed 3D skeleton & mesh in a metric world map overlay.
Comparison chart: trade-offs (portability, occlusion robustness, global consistency) vs. prior approaches.
paper_title: RoSHI: A Versatile Robot-oriented Suit for Human Data In-the-Wild
paper_authors: Wenjing Margaret Mao, Jefferson Ng, Luyang Hu, Daniel Gehrig, Antonio Loquercio
